pr_title: Overhaul Codebase to Avoid Static App.CurrentInstance
pr_body:
This PR is the culmination of lots of work I put into improving the app's codebase by removing/replacing our use of static App.CurrentInstance. This makes certain controls inside the project more modular as they no longer have inside knowledge of the current selected app instance. While this is a large step forward, this PR currently exists for review purposes and has no guarantee of being merged. Please test as much of the app's functionality as possible to find edge cases, because things may not be what they seem with these changes alone.

What I'm aware of:
- FIXED: ~~**Broken workaround for ModernNavigationToolbar and StatusBarControl**: Functionality on these controls is broken until we can implement the Commands properly.~~
- FIXED: ~~**Displayed path briefly flickers an incorrect value**: This only seems to happen when navigating back/forward~~
- OK: ~~**Opening or closing many tabs at once will lead to an unhandled exception**: We need to figure our a way to throttle tab creation/removal to be one at a time.~~
- FIXED: ~~**Opening the properties dialog will crash the app**~~

Fixes #16.

I will also look forward to hearing your feedback on the more technical aspects of this codebase change. If something seems out of place, we'd ideally want to document/correct it before this PR is merged.
pr_comments:
Noticed one issue:
- if you minimize and than restore the app anything that invokes the fulltrust process will crash the app with a `System.ObjectDisposedException` on `AppServiceConnection.SendMessageAsync`
Before the AppServiceConnection was recreated in the `OnLeavingBackground` when restoring the app

@gave92 Thanks for pointing this out. I noticed this also, and assumed that I fixed it by registering the OnLeavingBackground to an event handler inside ItemViewModel.cs. Maybe we should check if the AppService is available a better way?

@duke7553 ~I think the only issue is that you added this check `if (this.Connection == null)` in OnLeavingBackground which is only true the first time. I think somewhere we forgot to put `Connection = null` when the connection is being closed~
Edit: issue is that reassigning the AppServiceConnection in ItemViewModel will change it in ItemViewModel and ModernShellPage but not in BaseLayout maybe

@gave92 I added that check because the AppServiceConnection would occasionally display an exception that the Connection.OpenAsync() was executed at the wrong time. I assume that was because we tried to initialize the connection when one already exists.

issue_context.title: Add support for multiple Onedrive instances
issue_context.body:
Hey. I have both my work Onedrive and personal Onedrive on my computer. Could I have separate instances for it?

Also, SharePoint support would be great.

Great app!
comments: Hello, I'm working on a solution for this. In the mean time, try the solution listed here to see if Files Recognizes and displays the mapped drive. https://www.laptopmag.com/articles/map-onedrive-network-drive

While multiple sessions for One Drive is a great suggestion, it's not the same with the SharePoint. Because when you use something other than SharePoint you lose several capabilities like metadata, tags, indexing attributes, ACLs, versioning etc.

I have come across a shell extension called [SharePoint Shell Extensions](https://sse.technology/). The way they make use of metadata and other features SharePoint provides seems efficient. That eliminates the disadvantages I have mentioned [before](https://github.com/duke7553/files-uwp/issues/16#issuecomment-500157419).
Support for multiple OneDrive accounts will be implemented with #2215.

review_comments: Removing this once and for all felt sooooo good.
